text: What is the primary advantage of Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA) over Data-Dependent Acquisition (DDA) in proteomics?
choices: DIA requires no chromatographic separation prior to mass spectrometry
DIA systematically fragments all precursors within defined m/z windows, avoiding the stochastic top-N precursor selection of DDA
DIA only works with MALDI ionization sources
DIA eliminates the need for any spectral library or database during data analysis
explanation: DIA systematically isolates and fragments every precursor within a series of m/z windows, in contrast to DDA's stochastic selection of the top N most intense precursors, which improves reproducibility and reduces the missing-value problem across runs. DIA still requires LC separation, is not tied to any particular ionization source, and typically still relies on a spectral library (built from DDA runs or predicted in silico) to interpret the resulting composite spectra.
